scope: Fermionic two-particle vacuum loss and bounded interacting processing; research status only.

claims.statement: For a normalized pure two-form with canonical pair weights w_j>=0, sum_j w_j=1, set a=(1-eta)^2, b=eta^2, u=b/a, P(x)=product_j(1+x w_j), and solve P(x)=1+u. For the N100 sector-faithful convex-Gaussian completion, delta=a(u-x)=T(rho_eta,sigma_eta). If 0<=eta<1/2, delta <= a(1-sum_j w_j^2)[u+(1-u)ln(1-u)]. Its leading small-eta coefficient is e2=(1-sum_j w_j^2)/2, so delta=e2*b^2/a+O(b^3/a^2). Rank-one inputs have delta=0 exactly.
assumptions: Explicit pure two-fermion input and acquired canonical pair amplitudes.
Independent vacuum loss with particle survival probability eta; environment and loss flag discarded.
The bound is asserted only for eta<1/2.
claims.proof_path: REPORT.md, section 'New quantitative sharpening: pair-spectrum-dependent tail'. Use binomial(k,2)e_k=sum_{i<j}w_iw_j e_{k-2}(w_except_i_j)<=e2 and sum_{k>=2}x^k/binomial(k,2)=2[x+(1-x)ln(1-x)].
claims.novelty_boundary: An elementary shape-sensitive sharpening of N100's uniform bound, not a separate N100 headline and not a priority claim. Four-mode convex-Gaussian geometry is established prior art; exhaustive review is open.
costs: Acquire binomial(m,2) two-form coefficients and canonical decomposition.
Compute pair weights and scalar root x with bit precision charged, including log(1/a).
For many blocks, sum per-block errors and separately charge the Gaussian sampler.
claims.falsifier: A nonnegative normalized weight vector and eta<1/2 violating the envelope, or an error in the symmetric-polynomial identity or series sum.
claims.next_gate: Independent specialist proof review followed by a priority check against four-mode trace-distance and robustness results.

claims.statement: For an m-mode code C with k>0 and Majorana distance d_F>=3, n balanced standard lossy four-mode resources rho_eta_i, and deterministic unitary U consisting of Gaussian unitaries and g Tang-model gates exp(i theta_j Q_j) with even Majorana weight(Q_j)<=q, q>=4, the specified codeword fidelity is <=min{A*Theta_gq(C), Theta_gq(C)+Delta}. Here A=product_i(1+R_i) is the N102 robustness factor, Delta=1-product_i(1-delta_i) is the N100 completion distance, and Theta_gq(C) is Tang et al. Theorem 2's bound on (g,q)-doped Gaussian codeword fidelity. Hence fidelity >=1-epsilon requires Theta_gq(C)>=max{(1-epsilon)/A,1-epsilon-Delta}.
assumptions: Independent unobserved vacuum loss; no loss record.
N102 positive Gaussian domination holds for each balanced standard block.
The whole output system, including any Gaussian ancillas, is retained in deterministic unitary preparation; no postselection or measurement discard.
Every non-Gaussian gate exactly matches Tang et al.'s bounded-weight Majorana-product phase-gate model.
The supplied N100/N102 derivations and Tang et al. arXiv:2609.15059v1 Theorem 2 are valid.
claims.proof_path: REPORT.md, section 'Conditional interaction-versus-loss code bound'. Tensor N102 operator domination; each pure Gaussian mixture component after U belongs to Tang's (g,q)-doped family; apply Tang's overlap theorem and N100 trace-distance comparison.
claims.novelty_boundary: N105 uses only Tang's g=0 specialization. This composes the full g-dependent theorem only for deterministic unitary preparation. It does not cover interacting postselection, discarding, arbitrary interactions, or hardware noise. Priority and independent correctness remain open.
costs: Charge g, q, Gaussian circuit description, interaction angle precision, and supplied code parameters m,k,d_F.
Acquire the lossy two-form resource descriptions needed to compute each R_i.
This is a resource inequality, not a code-preparation algorithm or hardware energy estimate.
claims.falsifier: An allowed deterministic circuit and Gaussian component input whose codeword overlap exceeds Tang's stated bound, or a failure of tensor positivity/data processing.
claims.next_gate: Independent audit of Tang's theorem interface and this composition, especially the no-postselection/no-discard boundary.

claims.statement: The four-mode pure Gaussian state (|0000>+|1100>+|0011>+|1111>)/2 is mapped by V=exp(i*pi*n_1*n_3) to (|0000>+|1100>+|0011>-|1111>)/2. The output violates the four-mode Gaussian Plucker relation, so interacting processing need not preserve convex-Gaussianity.
assumptions: V is a quartic density-density interaction.
claims.proof_path: REPORT.md, section 'Counterexample and boundaries'. The input is a product of BCS pairs; V phases only |1111>; output Plucker sides are -1/4 and +1/4.
claims.novelty_boundary: Scope counterexample only; it proves neither computational hardness nor a large post-interaction resource lower bound.
costs: One four-mode quartic density-density interaction, charged as a non-Gaussian gate.
claims.falsifier: A correction to the stated Plucker relation or to the action of V on the occupation components.
claims.next_gate: Require an explicit gate-count and output-access model for any stronger interacting simulation claim.
